result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings:

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02 | Applied 4% instead of 3% | 3% |
| 54 | Applied 8% instead of 7% | 7% |
| 72 | Applied 6% instead of 5% | 5% |
| 27, 145 | Capped the price before taking the percentage, not the discount itself | Discount computed first, then capped |
| 32 | Started discounting at 13 units instead of 12 | `qty >= 12` |
| 105, 106, 146 | Used `>` so the discount was skipped exactly at the threshold | `>=` |
| 67 | Rounded the discount with `round` instead of rounding down to the won | Floor division (`//`) |
| 128, 142 | Only applied the 50,000-won cap when the discount went over 100,000 | Cap always applied |

To check, I parsed every docstring into the expected calculation and ran all 150 rules against it for quantities 0–299 and a range of unit prices. No rule differs anymore.

STATUS: DONE
